# class: memory | disk | hang-guard | cadence | safety | alarm | display | expiry | compaction | routing | leased-box | rationing | money | target

# verdict: KEEP = stays, class is not rationing · DROP = remove now (owner column names the open-asks row) · DEAD = the file applies to no unit or daemon, remove it · VOID = Joe voided the value, no live enforcement should remain · CHECK = owner names the class: rationing → DROP, anything else → KEEP with the measured reason

# RULES (#195): no rationing limits and no budget limit; a cap whose only reason is saving tokens or spend is DROP. Leased-box caps are DROP (only permanent Hetzner boxes since 10-11). Memory, disk, hang-guard and safety caps stay with their measured reason.

# A host-local rename (.off-by-N) does not remove a tracked drop-in: fleet-sync re-links it from ~/dotfiles (orch 60-quota-stretch.conf re-linked 10-31 10:32 PM PDT). A cap is removed by deleting it in the tracked file.

# v2 columns (P28 five-whys 11-01, mechanism 2): premise = the condition this cap rests on (empty = unconditional); expires = ISO date after which the cap is a lint violation if still live; applied_by = joe-<date> #<approvals> that set the value.
